questions.cardText:
[Law] What is the maximum prison sentence in Portugal?
A. 25 years B. 150 years C. 500 years
Answer: A. Portugal abolished life imprisonment in 1884. The current maximum prison sentence is set at 25 years, reflecting Portugal’s focus on rehabilitation over incarceration (expression of the re-educative function of punishment).
questions.de: Portugal schaffte 1884 die lebenslange Freiheitsstrafe ab. Wie hoch ist dort die Höchststrafe für eine Freiheitsstrafe?
questions.en: Portugal abolished life imprisonment in 1884. What is its maximum prison sentence?

timeline.labelEn: Portugal abolishes all forms of life imprisonment in the prison reforms of Sampaio e Melo
timeline.labelDe: Portugal schafft mit den Gefängnisreformen von Sampaio e Melo jede Form der lebenslangen Freiheitsstrafe ab

questions.cardText:
[Linguistic] What is the original meaning of “namaste” in Hindi?
A. I bow to you B. Bless soul C. Peace
Answer: A. The word “namaste” comes from Sanskrit as a combination of “namaḥ” (respect or homage) and “te” (to you). In Hindi, “namaḥ” also means “to bow” and thus “namaste” translates as “I bow to you.”
questions.de: Was bedeutet der Gruß „Namaste“ wörtlich, gebildet aus dem Sanskrit namaḥ (Verbeugung, Ehrerbietung) und te (dir)?
questions.en: What is the literal meaning of the greeting "namaste", from Sanskrit namaḥ (bow, homage) and te (to you)?

timeline.labelEn: The Rigveda, whose hymns already use namas, "bow, reverence", the root of namaste
timeline.labelDe: Der Rigveda, dessen Hymnen bereits namas („Verbeugung, Ehrerbietung“) verwenden, die Wurzel von Namaste

questions.notes: The word is Sanskrit, used in Hindi and other Indian languages. Accept close renderings such as "bowing to you" or "I bow to the divine in you"; namaḥ also means homage or adoration.
